weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Build the answer on the golden-calf evidence (they saw God and still turned away) and cut the stacked quotes (Pascal plus John 20:29) and the channel tagline, ending on one real question.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis itself (one prohibition among 'of every tree thou mayest freely eat', the tree of life also there) instead of the Ten Commandments analogy, which comes centuries later.
Cut the colleague and job-loss analogy and use that time on the Peter-versus-Judas contrast, which is the real payoff.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Actually answer the hook: show from Exodus 12 what the blood meant (a lamb died in the firstborn's place; 'the blood shall be to you for a token'; Israel was not exempt by birth) and cut the Exodus backstory recap.

weakest_line: Let's look at Samson, known as the strongest man in the Bible.
one_fix: State the takeaway plainly (being used by God is not the same as being approved by God) and make the closing question about that, not a meta 'what surprised you more' poll.

weakest_line: Work in that world would feel like tending something you love.
one_fix: Anchor each 'what would be different' claim in a specific text detail (Genesis 2:15 work before the fall, the tree of life still open) and drop the C. S. Lewis quote and channel tagline.

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Build the whole video around Cornelius (God sent the message to the seeker's door), cut the three-part list and the Sodom digression, and end with a question that does not assume the viewer is a believer.

weakest_line: It's one of the most asked questions about the Bible and most Christians can't answer it.
one_fix: Replace 'you'll know what to say' with a real question to the viewer built on the 'one blood, every person is family' idea, so the ending invites a response.
Open on the puzzle in the text ('God knew exactly where Adam was, so why ask "Where art thou?"') instead of a sermon question aimed at the viewer's own sin.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Answer the 'forever' part of the hook with real text evidence instead of a numbered run of familiar invitation verses (John 10:10, Revelation 3:20) quoted out of context.
